summary: The patch correctly fixes the misleading AttributeError: when a class-level descriptor (e.g. a property) raises AttributeError internally, it now re-dispatches via object.__getattribute__ so the real underlying error surfaces instead of masking it as 'prop' missing. Logic is correct, minimal, and recursion-safe since object.__getattribute__ does not re-trigger __getattr__.

issues.description: The new branch relies on the subtle fact that object.__getattribute__ (unlike the type-level lookup hook) does not fall back to __getattr__, so a descriptor's internal AttributeError propagates instead of recursing. A short comment explaining this intent would aid future maintainers.

The original '# Fail' comment now sits inside the if-branch and the success path (return object.__getattribute__) is uncommented; a one-line note on why re-dispatch is needed would improve readability.
